_note: filename -> CSS object-position, read by scripts/build_banners.py and
published into docs/data/panel/banners.json as 'focal'. It is where the
page crops THIS image when the masthead's height cap bites.
HOW EACH ONE WAS SET, so the next person can redo it rather than guess:
every banner was overlaid with a 5% horizontal grid and the face band was
read off it -- top of the highest hat or hairline to the lowest chin. The
y value is then the smallest object-position that puts the window's top
edge a few percent ABOVE that band at the widest desktop band (1360px,
where the crop is deepest). Narrower viewports crop less, so a value that
clears the faces at 1360 clears them everywhere.
x is 50% on every one and that is not laziness: the band is never
squarer than the art, so object-fit never crops horizontally. The x
component is carried because object-position needs two.
Absent is legal -- app.js falls back to '50% 22%', which biases toward
the top because these are group portraits.
